meta.title: Parallel-plate capacitor: fringing fields by finite differences
meta.tools: 2-D finite-difference Laplace solver (eelab.laplace), energy method, Palmer's fringing formula
meta.summary: Compute the capacitance of finite parallel plates numerically, show how the fringing field makes it exceed εA/d, and compare the excess with Palmer's analytic fringing correction.
meta.problem: εA/d is the first capacitance formula everyone learns. When is it wrong, and by how much?
meta.theory:
Ideal: $C'=\varepsilon w/d$ (per unit depth). Fringing adds capacitance at the edges; Palmer (1927) for 2-D plates of width w, gap d:
$C'\approx\frac{\varepsilon w}{d}\left[1+\frac{d}{\pi w}+\frac{d}{\pi w}\ln\frac{2\pi w}{d}\right]$. For w/d = 10 the correction is ≈ 16 %; it vanishes as w/d → ∞.
meta.method: Plates ±0.5 V, thickness one cell, in a 12w × 12w grounded box, Δ = d/20. w/d = 1, 2, 5, 10, 20. C′ from field energy.
